chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites Surah al-Taghabun in his obligatory prayer will have it intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection, and serve as a just witness before one who accepts its testimony; it will not leave him until he enters Paradise.

key_terms.سُورَةَ التَّغَابُنِ: Surah al-Taghabun (The Day of Mutual Disavowal), the 64th chapter of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Taghabun in obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the enduring spiritual efficacy of reciting Surah al-Taghabun during obligatory prayers, portraying it as a permanent companion to the believer. The text highlights its dual role as an intercessor (*shafi'ah*) and a truthful witness (*shahid al-adl*) on the Day of Judgment, a concept rooted in the Shia understanding of Quranic verses as active agents in salvation. This specific merit underscores the tradition's view that consistent recitation embeds the Surah’s themes of divine decree and human accountability into the soul, ensuring it does not depart until the believer enters Paradise.
